title: TreeMap: Sorted Maps & Range Queries
summary: Master TreeMap: NavigableMap interface, subMap, headMap, tailMap range queries, lowerKey, higherKey, and key ordering guarantees.
prerequisites: The Map Contract: Associative Key-Value Storage
learningObjectives: Master the Red-Black tree architecture and NavigableMap contract of TreeMap
Utilize logarithmic range and slice views: subMap(), headMap(), and tailMap()
Execute boundary and proximity lookups: floorEntry(), ceilingEntry(), higherKey(), lowerKey()
Contrast natural key ordering with custom Comparator implementations
expectedOutcomes: Ability to architect range-based lookups (e.g. tax brackets, IP subnets, scheduling) with O(log N) efficiency
Mastery of bidirectional map traversal and bounded sub-map mutation semantics

activities.title: Practical Context: Progressive Tax Bracket Classification

analogy.headline: Practical Context: Progressive Tax Bracket Classification
analogy.story:
In national revenue systems, tax rates are defined in tier brackets: Income up to $10,000 pays 10%; income from $10,001 to $50,000 pays 20%; income above $50,000 pays 30%.

When a citizen reports an income of $38,450, the tax system does not look for an exact hash match for '$38,450' (which would fail). Instead, it queries: 'Find the highest tax bracket threshold that is less than or equal to $38,450' (a floor lookup).

A hash table cannot answer range questions because hash functions scatter numbers randomly. A TreeMap maintains keys in total sorted order, resolving range brackets in logarithmic O(log N) time.
analogy.keyTakeaway: TreeMap maintains keys in sorted order inside a Red-Black Tree, enabling O(log N) proximity searches, ceiling/floor lookups, and range slices.

activities.title: TreeMap Architecture: Red-Black Trees & NavigableMap Range Queries

keyTakeaways: TreeMap implements NavigableMap and SortedMap, backed by a balanced Red-Black Tree
Keys must implement Comparable or be governed by an explicit Comparator provided in the constructor
Guarantees O(log N) time complexity for containsKey, get, put, and remove
Exposes rich proximity and range methods: floorEntry(), ceilingEntry(), subMap(), descendingMap()

activities.title: IP Subnet Geographic Routing Engine
activities.description: Trace a network router finding the closest network gateway using TreeMap floorKey lookups.

steps.description: Instantiate a NavigableMap<Long, String> backed by TreeMap to maintain IP address blocks in sorted numerical order.
Invoke floorKey(targetIp) to locate the subnet start address less than or equal to the target IP in O(log N) time.
Test with an IP inside the 10.0.0.0 block, correctly routing to US_EAST_GATEWAY.

questions.question: What is the time complexity of map.get(key) and map.put(key, val) in a TreeMap?
questions.explanation: Because TreeMap is backed by a self-balancing Red-Black binary search tree, all basic operations have guaranteed logarithmic O(log N) complexity.

questions.question: What happens when map.put(null, 'value') is executed on a default TreeMap?
options: The null key is placed at the root
The value is stored at index 0
questions.explanation: TreeMap must compare the key to other keys in the tree using compareTo(). Calling null.compareTo() throws NullPointerException.

questions.question: What does map.floorEntry(key) return?
options: The entry with the greatest key strictly less than key
The entry with the greatest key less than or equal to the given key, or null if no such key exists
The least key strictly greater than key
The root entry of the tree
questions.explanation: floorEntry returns the entry associated with the greatest key less than or equal to the given key (inclusive).

questions.question: How are duplicate keys handled in a TreeMap?
options: Duplicate keys are detected via key1.equals(key2)
Duplicate keys are detected when comparator.compare(key1, key2) == 0 (or key1.compareTo(key2) == 0)
Duplicate keys are stored in a linked list
questions.explanation: TreeMap relies strictly on its Comparator / Comparable. If compare returns 0, the existing value is replaced, regardless of whether equals() returns true.

questions.question: When would you choose TreeMap over HashMap in production backend systems?
questions.answer: Choose TreeMap when: 1) Range queries or bounded slices (subMap, headMap, tailMap) are required, 2) Nearest-match proximity queries are needed (finding closest price, timestamp, or IP gateway via floorKey/ceilingKey), 3) Keys must be iterated in natural or custom sorted order (e.g. generating alphabetical directories or financial reports), or 4) Predictable worst-case O(log N) latency is strictly preferred over hash table spikes during rehash resizes.

questions.question: Is the subMap returned by TreeMap a deep copy or a backed view?
questions.answer: It is a backed view. Changes made to the original TreeMap within the range are immediately reflected in the subMap, and modifications made to the subMap write directly to the parent TreeMap. If you attempt to insert an entry into a subMap outside its specified key boundaries, an IllegalArgumentException is thrown.

questions.question: What is the consequence of compareTo() being inconsistent with equals() when using TreeMap?
questions.answer: The Map contract specifies that uniqueness is governed by equals(), but TreeMap violates this by relying on compareTo() == 0. If compareTo() returns 0 for two keys that are not equal according to equals() (e.g., comparing Employees solely by salary), inserting the second Employee will overwrite the first Employee's value! To prevent silent data loss, compareTo() must always be consistent with equals().

activities.title: Self-Evaluation: TreeMap & Range Queries
checklist: I understand the Red-Black tree mechanics providing O(log N) guarantees in TreeMap
I know how to execute floorKey(), ceilingKey(), and subMap() range queries
I understand why null keys are disallowed and how compareTo() defines uniqueness in TreeMap

practiceProblems.title: Find Tax Rate by Income
practiceProblems.problemStatement: Given a TreeMap<Double, Double> mapping income thresholds to tax rates, implement getTaxRate(TreeMap<Double, Double> brackets, double income) that returns the rate using floorEntry(). If income is negative, return 0.0.
hints: Check entry != null before calling getValue().

practiceProblems.title: Extract Score Range Map
practiceProblems.problemStatement: Given a TreeMap<Integer, String> mapping scores to student names, return a Map containing only students with scores between minScore and maxScore (both inclusive).
hints: Use scores.subMap(min, true, max, true) for inclusive boundaries.

practiceProblems.title: Find Closest Preceding Event
practiceProblems.problemStatement: Given a TreeMap<Long, String> mapping event timestamps to event names, implement findPrecedingEvent(TreeMap<Long, String> events, long queryTime) that returns the event with the highest timestamp < queryTime, or 'NONE' if no such event exists.
hints: lowerEntry(queryTime) returns the entry strictly less than queryTime.

practiceProblems.title: Custom Comparator by String Length
practiceProblems.problemStatement: Create a TreeMap<String, Integer> with a custom Comparator that orders keys by length ascending, breaking ties alphabetically.
practiceProblems.expectedOutput: TreeMap ordered by length then natural

practiceProblems.title: Reverse-Order Price Book
practiceProblems.problemStatement: Given a TreeMap<Double, String> mapping prices to item names, return a descending-order view of the map.
